Commentary.Commentary: We are back for England's reply! We can see the Indian player make their way out to the middle and spread out to take their respective field positions. Mohammed Siraj looks fit and is taking the field. There is a slight halt as the hosts have come out with the second new ball. It has been replaced now and we are good to go. Zak Crawley and Ben Duckett are the two openers for England. Jasprit Bumrah to start proceedings with the ball. Also, as India were given a penalty for Ravichandran Ashwin running down the middle of the pitch, the visitors will be starting at 5/0. Let's play...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

England, on the other hand, would not be satisfied with their performance as they could have cut down a lot of runs if they had taken the catches when they presented themselves. Joe Root dropping Rohit Sharma on 27 did not help them at all while they spilled a few in this session as well. Mark Wood put in a herculean effort and was the pick of the bowlers with four wickets. They started off the day really well but were not able to capitalise on the start provided by their bowlers. Now, the blasting English batting lineup has the task of putting 445 in front of them on a wicket that is still very good for the batters. England will be looking to start well after the break and get most of the runs till the time the wicket plays well. They have been aggressive with the bat and will carry on the batting in the same way. The second inning is coming up soon, so stay tuned.

With that, we come to the end of the Indian first innings and India has managed to score 445 after batting for 130.5 overs and will be really happy with their total. The skipper Rohit Sharma led from the front, scoring a brilliant 131 off 196 ball that included 14 boundaries and 3 sixes. Along with him, the Indian all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja posted 112 off 225 balls with the support of the two debutants, Sarfaraz Khan who scored a brilliant 62 and Dhruv Jurel scoring 46 and getting the Indian side to 445 runs in the first innings of this Test Match.

England, buoyed by the early breakthroughs, came out all guns blazing in the first hour of play, displaying discipline and tactical acumen with the ball. As the players retreat to the pavilion for a well-deserved Lunch break, India will take solace in their resilient showing, knowing that they are well-placed to post a formidable total in their first innings. However, the decision to promote Ravindra Jadeja up the order proved to be a stroke of genius, as he and skipper Rohit Sharma orchestrated a remarkable recovery with a substantial partnership. Both batters notched brilliant centuries, while debutant Sarfaraz Khan showcased his talent with a sparkling half-century before an unfortunate run-out. Hello and welcome to our coverage of Day 2 of the 3rd Test between India and England. Day 1 was packed with entertainment and excitement. While the visitors initially seized control of the game, they failed to capitalize on their advantage, allowing the hosts to stage a remarkable comeback. Right then, India have runs on the board and still have more than enough wickets to target 450 runs from here. One positive for England is that the wicket in all certainty will be even better for batting on Day 2 and if they bundle out India early enough, they would be able to bat in excellent conditions. A fascinating Day 2 will begin on Friday at 9.30 am IST (4 am GMT) but you can join us sooner for the build-up. Cheers!

England on the other end will not be entirely pleased with how things ended on Day 1 given they had the hosts on a string in the first 10 overs of the game. Mark Wood was their best bowler and even in the final session, he looked the most likely to pick up a wicket and he did exactly that by sending back the Indian skipper with a well-planned maneuver. England failed to capitalize though and allowed the debutant to play his shots and conceded quick runs. They also missed a couple of LBW calls on which they could have taken the DRS and got rid of both Rohit Sharma and Ravindra Jadeja which did prove costly. However, a lucky chance fell their way and it was Mark Wood yet again but made sure to get the direct hit in and that got them the wicket of Sarfaraz Khan. The second new ball was taken very late in the day and they will hope to do some early damage with it on Day 2.

Session Summary - 34 overs, 141 runs and 2 wickets. What a stellar final session on Day 1 and the runs really flowed late in the day. India began the post-Tea session with two set batters on the crease and both looked to accelerate a bit. Rohit Sharma got a barrage of short balls and dealt with them well until one that he really snatched at and got out on 131. The highly-rated debutant, Sarfaraz Khan then took to the crease and soon enough, he started taking on the spinners. Khan was aggressive and raked up boundaries for fun with Ravindra Jadeja a mere spectator at the other end. Khan brought up his 50 and looked good but was a bit unfortunate to have gotten run out with just a few overs remaining. Jadeja went on to notch up his 4th Test ton and India ended the day with still half of their wickets intact.

On the other hand, England opted for a combination of pace and spin with Hartley and Anderson leading the attack and bowled in tandem for almost the first thirty minutes. Despite their efforts, the English bowlers struggled to break through the partnership. While Anderson consistently targeted the batsmen with deliveries angling in, he found no success. Hartley, although extracting some assistance from the pitch, couldn't quite trouble the batsmen with his spin during the initial hour of the session. Stokes tossed the ball to Joe Root and Rehan Ahmed right before the end of the session. But the Indian batters were too comfortable facing them and the English bowlers didn't produce any wickets in the session, making it the first session of the series to go wicketless.

TEA, DAY 1 - SESSION SUMMARY - 27 Overs, 92 Runs, 0 Wickets. The post-lunch session draws to a close as players now head off for Tea on Day 1. A good session from an Indian perspective. Despite facing the setback of losing three early wickets in the preceding session, Rohit Sharma and Ravindra Jadeja displayed remarkable concentration and composure as they strengthened their partnership. Negotiating the conditions adeptly, they confidently rotated the strike and patiently maneuvered the deliveries. With the session progressing, the batting conditions notably improved, enabling Sharma to capitalize on loose deliveries with well-timed boundaries and a six. Together, they constructed a resilient partnership of 100 runs. After the drinks break, Rohit took a bit of an aggressive route and added quick runs to the tally. Ravindra Jadeja too partnered him well scoring a Fifty, and they both remain unbeaten on 97 and 68 respectively.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session on Day 1! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of England. England went with the option to play two seamers and that decision proved to be a positive one as Mark Wood did some early damage with his searing pace. Wood sent back the double-centurion and the centurion from the last game after which Tom Hartley came in and capitalized with a wicket of his own. The visitors had India on the ropes and James Anderson bowled a lovely second spell, troubling the Indian skipper on multiple occasions but it was Hartley who induced the outside edge only for Joe Root to spill it and that missed opportunity has allowed Rohit Sharma to score a half-century. England have picked up early wickets on a surface that is excellent for batting but it is now about avoiding the bad deliveries and keeping things tight. Do join us for the fascinating post-Lunch session at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT).

SESSION SUMMARY - 25 overs, 93 runs and 3 wickets. End of a highly intriguing first session on Day 1 of the 3rd Test match in Rajkot and at the Lunch interval, England will surely be the happier of the two sides. India started off quickly with Yashasvi Jaiswal picking up a couple of early boundaries and Rohit Sharma looked positive too but soon enough, Jaiswal was dismissed and Shubman Gill followed suit just a couple of overs later. Rajat Patidar came in and hung around for a bit but he was also dismissed and India were reeling at 33/3 inside the first 9 overs. With two debutants slotted to come next, it was the local boy, Ravindra Jadeja who was sent up the order to regain a bit of control. The Indian skipper looked very tentative and got a big life as well but he slowly started to play his shots. Late in the first session, both batters put away the bad balls and we got to see how good a batting surface it really is.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to start the 3rd Test! We can see the England players make their way out to the middle and spread out to take their respective field positions. Yashasvi Jaiswal and Rohit Sharma are the two openers for India with the former facing the first ball. James Anderson has the new cherry in his hand and he is going with three slips and a gully. Let's play...

As skipper Rohit Sharma mentioned earlier, there are a couple of debutants in the Indian team. So, before the start of the match, Anil Kumble handed Sarfaraz Khan his Test cap while Dinesh Karthik handed the other to Dhruv Jurel.

Ben Stokes, the captain of England says that he would have batted first as well. Adds that yes, time flies given it is his 100th Test match and he wants to have fun. Mentions that they are happy with how things have gone in the first two Tests and the boys have done well. On the trip to the UAE, he says that they didn't play cricket and rather spent their time with their families. Adds that the great thing about Test matches is that both teams get a chance and they want to continue in the same fashion. Ends by informing that Mark Wood is back in for Shoaib Bashir.

The Indian skipper, Rohit Sharma says that they will bat first. Adds that it looks like a good pitch, surely better than the last two. Tells that Rajkot is known to be a good wicket and it will deteriorate as the game goes on and they want to put the runs on the board. Mentions that someone or the other hand stepped up for them when needed and he is sure that there will be no shortage of excitement in the next three Tests as well. Informs they have made four changes. Sarfaraz Khan and Dhruv Jurel make their debuts, Axar Patel and Mukesh Kumar miss out as Ravindra Jadeja and Mohammed Siraj come in.
England (Playing XI) - Zak Crawley, Ben Duckett, Ollie Pope, Joe Root, Jonny Bairstow, Ben Stokes (C), Ben Foakes (WK), Rehan Ahmed, Tom Hartley, Mark Wood (In for Shoaib Bashir), James Anderson.

India (Playing XI) - Yashasvi Jaiswal, Rohit Sharma (C), Shubman Gill, Rajat Patidar, Sarfaraz Khan (On Test debut, in for Shreyas Iyer), Ravindra Jadeja (In for Axar Patel), Dhruv Jurel (On Test debut, in for KS Bharat) (WK), Ravichandran Ashwin, Kuldeep Yadav, Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj (In for Mukesh Kumar).
TOSS - India have won the toss and they will BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Nick Knight and Deep Dasgupta are pitchside. Knight says that the pitch looks excellent for batting and adds that there are a lot of cracks on it but there is a green tinge that will help the seamers. DDS joins him and says that the spinners will not get much help in the first couple of days. Mentions that there is moisture on it along with black cotton soil and it is a really good batting wicket as the crack won't open up early on.

Ben Stokes is set to make history as he plays his 100th Test match, joining an elite group of 16 England players to achieve this milestone. Despite initial doubts, England silenced critics with a remarkable win in the first Test and put up a strong fight in the second. This English side has demonstrated resilience and determination, with young talents like Rehan Ahmed and Tom Hartley making notable contributions. Mark Wood will replace Shoaib Bashir for the upcoming game, supporting the veteran James Anderson, who continues to defy age. England's batters have shown grit against the spin threat, but they'll be hoping for more conversions of starts to pose an even greater challenge to the hosts. With India grappling with injury concerns, England sees an opportune moment to secure another Test win on Indian soil. Let's see if any of the side makes it 2-1 or not. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

India will once again be without their star batter, Virat Kohli who is confirmed out for the entire series, and experienced KL Rahul adding to the challenge for captain Rohit Sharma. Leading the side amidst various injury concerns, Sharma also faces the pressure of scoring runs himself. The third Test may see a couple of players making their debut in the form of Sarfaraz Khan and Dhruv Jurel as India looks to change a few things around in the middle order. Yashasvi Jaiswal has been a standout performer with the bat for the hosts, while Jasprit Bumrah's exceptional bowling stands out as a highlight, especially considering the dominance of spinners in the series. The team is hopeful that Ravindra Jadeja will be fit to play, adding to their depth, and Shubman Gill's confidence is expected to soar after his century in the previous game. With momentum on their side, the Men in Blue aims for consecutive victories to assert their dominance.

Hello and a warm welcome, everyone! The arrival of Bazball in India has certainly stirred up excitement, and it's safe to say that it has made quite an impression. With the series level at 1-1 after the first two Tests, cricket enthusiasts have been treated to plenty of thrilling moments, and there's no shortage of entertainment in sight. As we gear up for the third Test, all eyes are on the Niranjan Shah Stadium in Rajkot. Both teams will be leaving no stone unturned as they strive to seize the lead in the series. Anticipation is high, and fans can expect another intense battle between these two formidable cricketing nations.
